messages.subject: Robust t-distribution in regression models
parts:
Hi everyone!

I would like to know if it is possible to change prior normal-distribution to t-distribution in 'blavaan'. I have some data with non-normal distribution because the presence of ouliers.

Thanks a lot,

Danilo

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Robust t-distribution in regression models
parts:
Danilo,

This is not possible with the current version of blavaan, though it can get you close if you are willing to edit the JAGS code yourself. 

To do this, I would fit the traditional model (with normal distributions) using blavaan, using the argument jagfile=TRUE. This exports the JAGS code. Towards the top of the JAGS code, you will see a line that says something like

y[i,j] ~ dnorm(mu[i,j], invtheta[j,g[i]])

If you edit that line to be y[i,j] ~ dt(mu[i,j], invtheta[j,g[i], ...), then you should be able to estimate the model (but you will have to fill in the "..." to deal with the degrees of freedom parameter). This will not give you the blavaan fitMeasures, but you can at least estimate the model. For more information on using the exported JAGS code, see the bottom of p. 14 here:

http://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.05604v1.pdf


Ed

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Robust t-distribution in regression models
parts:
Gwern,

I could be wrong, but I believe Danilo is talking about the distribution of each observed variable, as opposed to the prior on a model parameter. That is, he wants the conditional distribution of y given the latent variables to be t instead of normal. But you are correct that you can use a t distribution as a prior on any model parameter (either through dpriors() or through the prior() modifier in the model syntax).

Ed

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Robust t-distribution in regression models
parts:
Currently, you can only do this by editing the JAGS code and running it yourself (see the manuscript that I referenced in my previous post).

The problem is that, when you use the t distribution to model y, then the model likelihood does not fit into the traditional SEM likelihoods implemented in (b)lavaan. So blavaan currently cannot evaluate this new likelihood to provide fit measures, etc. But you can still obtain posterior parameter estimates via JAGS.

Ed
